title: CPU Optimizations (Library of Ruina)
description: CPU savings for the game's per-frame work. The loop fix removes a pointless loop in the Unity binding that copies native GetComponents results into a managed List: after the results are copied, the loop walked every unused slot up to the list's capacity and discarded the result, wasting CPU on every call (about 10% of main-thread samples, and 26% in late frames, in a Library of Ruina 1.0.3 capture). Four optional sub-settings cut more per-frame work: CharacterSpriteMaskController.Update (about 4.5% of main-thread samples) can sync its masks every other frame, the input module's mouse processing (about 4.9%) can be skipped while the touchscreen pointer is idle, ClipperRegistry.Cull (RectMask2D clipping and culling, about 21%) can run every other frame, and TextMeshProUGUI.InternalUpdate (the per-frame lossyScale read of every label, about 5%) can check each label every fourth frame. For Library of Ruina 1.0.3.

launcher.label: CPU Optimizations
launcher.note: Removes wasted CPU work the game does every frame, mainly while the UI rebuilds. Frees up processing power for smoother performance and lower heat.

settings.label: Throttle sprite mask updates
settings.note: Character sprite masks re-check their sprite renderer every frame. This does it every other frame, so a mask can follow a character's visibility one frame late.

settings.label: Skip idle pointer updates
settings.note: Skips the per-frame UI raycast while the touchscreen pointer is not moving or pressed, and still refreshes it about every 6 frames. Touchscreen Mode only.

settings.label: Throttle UI clipping
settings.note: Masked UI lists (RectMask2D) re-cull all their children every frame. This does it only every few frames (see the next setting), and every frame while masks are added or removed, so an item can enter a list's view a frame or two late.

settings.label: UI clipping interval
settings.note: Frames between UI clipping passes while Throttle UI clipping is on. 2 is every other frame; 4 saves the most CPU but an item can enter a list's view up to three frames late.

settings.label: Throttle text scale checks
settings.note: Every text label reads its world scale each frame to keep its edges sharp. This checks each label every fourth frame, so a label that is scaling can look slightly soft for up to three frames.

aeea627ddbd1214764dfef5f965e94a2.reason: CharacterSpriteMaskController.Update, just after mov w20, wzr that starts the enable-sync loop (every path into the loop passes it): x19 = the controller; the host writes w20 = 0x7fffffff to skip the loop on a throttled frame

LOR_InputModule.Process, after ldr x9 of the BaseInput.mousePresent virtual and before its blr: the host may swap x9 for a filter that returns false while the touchscreen pointer is idle, which skips ProcessMouseEvent
ClipperRegistry.Cull, the cmp w22, #1 right after w22 = the clippers' count: x19 = the registry; the host writes w22 = 0 on a throttled frame, which ends the function before its loop

TextMeshProUGUI.InternalUpdate, the mov x19, x0 between the load of m_havePropertiesChanged into w8 and its cbnz: x0 = the label; the host writes w8 = 1 on a throttled frame, which skips the lossyScale check
